# Inheritance Tax Explained

> Plain English explanations of UK inheritance tax, the April 2027 pension changes, annuities, whole of life assurance and trusts, with videos, key facts and full transcripts. Every answer links to the law and HMRC guidance it relies on. By Steve Hunt ACII TEP. Education only.

Author: Steve Hunt ACII TEP, Chartered Insurance Risk Manager and Trust and Estate Practitioner, in UK financial services since 1980.
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/steve~hunt
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@SteveHuntACIITEP

## Videos with key facts, sources and full transcripts

- [How will your pension be taxed when you die after April 2027?](https://inheritancetaxexplained.co.uk/pensions-and-inheritance-tax-from-april-2027/): From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and pension death benefits count as part of your estate for inheritance tax, and can be taxed at 40% on death. Pensions left to a spouse or civil partner stay exempt. Unmarried partners are not covered.
- [Nominees' annuity: what is it, how does it work, and what's the catch?](https://inheritancetaxexplained.co.uk/nominees-annuity/): A nominees' annuity is an annuity paid to a nominee of a pension member: someone the member nominates, such as an adult child or grandchild, who is not a dependant under the pension tax rules. This page is about the version bought in the member's lifetime, together with the member's own lifetime annuity, either as one joint life annuity or as a related separate contract. When the member dies, the income carries on to the nominee for the rest of their life. Nominees' annuities can also be bought after the member's death, but that is a different route, and not the one excluded from inheritance tax.
- [Whole of life assurance: what is it, why does a whole generation distrust it, and what has changed?](https://inheritancetaxexplained.co.uk/whole-of-life-assurance/): Whole of life assurance puts a monetary value on a person's life, the sum assured, and pays it out when that person dies, whenever that is, provided the premiums are paid. Under the Life Assurance Act 1774 you can only insure a life in which you have an insurable interest. An individual has an unlimited insurable interest in their own life and in the life of their spouse or civil partner.

## Guides: one subject, every question answered, with sources

- [The nominees' annuity: every question answered](https://inheritancetaxexplained.co.uk/nominees-annuity/guide/): A nominees' annuity is an annuity paid to someone a pension member nominates, such as an adult child or grandchild, who is not a dependant under the pension tax rules. Bought in the member's lifetime together with the member's own lifetime annuity, the income carries on to the nominee for the rest of their life when the member dies, and from 6 April 2027 it is excluded from the member's estate for inheritance tax.

Transcripts are not edited; dated notes sit beside any correction.
